expected:
# BUG-SEARCHHOSTS — searchHosts() output missing 'hostid', breaking the port-link/promote pickers

Discovered live via the actual browser UI (user report, not a planned campaign scenario),
during manual testing of B4 (manual link, host<->host variant). Written after the anomaly was
already understood from the screenshot (port-link picker on Switch1 showing "This host has no
ports reported" and a disabled Link button) but before re-confirming the exact root cause below.

Expected once suspected: the shared frontend (monitoring.topology.view.js.php, written against
CTopologyPrototype::searchHosts()'s {hostid, name, monitoring_state} shape) reads
target_host.hostid directly in both the promote-picker and the port-link-picker flows. If
CTopologyTModel::searchHosts() returns {id, name} instead (missing hostid), target_host.hostid
is undefined in both flows -- promote silently sends hostid=undefined, and the port-link
picker's follow-up ports.get call fetches id="h:undefined", which matches no host and returns
empty groups, exactly matching the screenshot.
actual: Confirmed: CTopologyTModel::searchHosts() returned only {id, name}, omitting 'hostid' -- the exact field the shared frontend reads (target_host.hostid) in both the port-link picker (Switch1's ports.get follow-up fetched 'h:undefined', hence 'This host has no ports reported' and a permanently-disabled Link button, per the user's own screenshot) and the promote picker (would have silently sent hostid=undefined to /promote). FIXED live (not deferred past the campaign, since this was reported as a direct usability blocker, not found via a scripted scenario) by adding 'hostid' to the returned array, matching CTopologyPrototype::searchHosts()'s shape exactly. Re-verified via tmodel_call.php: searchHosts('Switch1') now returns hostid='11252' alongside id='h:11252'.
notes: Fixed in ui/include/classes/topology/CTopologyTModel.php (searchHosts()). This is an exception to ground rule 1 (no implementation changes during the campaign) because it was reported as a live usability blocker mid-session, not discovered via a scripted scenario -- recorded here for completeness rather than silently fixed off the record.
